The gap

The problem is not simply access to more data. It is the absence of trusted pathways from evidence to action.

The world has produced marine science faster than anyone can use it. We understand these ecosystems better than at any point in history — and yet the people who decide their future often cannot reach that knowledge in time, in a form they can act on, when a choice is in front of them.

Nearly three decades of standardized reef monitoring. Official fisheries databases holding millions of records. Hundreds of reefs assessed with a peer-reviewed status index. Most of it still unreachable at the moment of decision.

Why it persists

A structural problem, not a failure of effort.

The gap has real, understandable causes — which is exactly why it can be closed.

Cause 01

Fragmented

Knowledge lives in monitoring programs, databases, and papers that were never built to speak to one another.

Cause 02

Slow to reach

Answering one real conservation question can take days of specialized database, statistical, and computational work.

Cause 03

Outpacing us

Complexity keeps rising while the time to decide keeps shrinking — beyond what any individual can hold at once.

The reframe

Not a better map of the problem. The missing layer beneath the decision.

A category that did not exist before

ChatMPA is scientific decision infrastructure for Marine Protected Areas.

Infrastructure is the layer institutions build on and come to depend on. It is invisible when it works, and it outlives any single product built upon it. ChatMPA is that missing layer between marine science and marine decisions.

The word scientific constrains the word decision: accountable to evidence, reproducible, and open to review. That constraint is the moat.

The principle

Human judgment leads. AI strengthens the process.

A division of responsibility that never changes — established before any capability is shown.

Artificial intelligenceaccelerates Integrates and synthesizes evidence at a speed no team could match.
Scientistsvalidate Guarantee the reasoning is sound and the uncertainty is stated honestly.
← the lead Managersdecide Weigh the trade-offs and own the choice, in front of a board or a community.
Institutionsgovern Hold the legal authority and the public accountability for what happens next.

We never ask AI to choose the right decision. We use it to organize evidence and make complex relationships legible. The human cannot be removed from the loop — because the loop is built around them.

A real decision

If temperature rises, productivity falls, and predator biomass drops — should a manager change fishing rules, tourism limits, or first find which driver is to blame?

This is the kind of question a Marine Protected Area faces in practice — and the reason integrated scientific reasoning matters. What follows is how ChatMPA turns questions like it into answers a manager can defend.

Rung 01 · Scientific memory Operational

“Which species have increased their landings over the past decade?”

Mexico's official fisheries database holds more than 10 million landing records in a complex relational structure — one of the world's largest fisheries datasets, yet out of reach without database, statistical, or programming skills. ChatMPA is building the Model Context Protocol that understands that structure, so any scientist, manager, or community can interrogate it in plain language — no schemas, SQL, or statistical software — while every result keeps its scientific traceability. Not a chatbot for fisheries: a scientific interface to the knowledge system itself. From isolated fisheries records → accessible scientific knowledge.

One database, opened by languageconceptual
Rung 02 · Ecosystem intelligence Active research

“Sea temperature rose while productivity fell. Is the fish decline climate — or fishing?”

ChatMPA connects nearly three decades of ecological monitoring with NASA Earth-observation data, so AI can reason across drivers in one framework — testing competing explanations instead of reporting a single trend. From fragmented monitoring → ecosystem intelligence.

Competing drivers, resolvedconceptual
Rung 03 · Decision intelligence Active research

“Should limited funding go to ecological restoration — or to local economic development?”

The Marine Prosperity Index evaluates how environment, economy, and society interact, and surfaces the single dimension limiting prosperity — turning static scores into decision-support that compares interventions and their trade-offs. From measuring sustainability → navigating prosperity.

The limiting dimensionconceptual
Rung 04 · Trustworthy scientific AI Controlled experiment

“If two analysts ask the same question and get different answers — which one do we trust?”

AI can be perfectly consistent and consistently wrong. ChatMPA encodes methodological judgment into structured, reviewable Skills — the unit of analysis, the method, the seeds, the checks. A controlled experiment across 400 runs, two languages, and five levels of detail shows the right Skill removes the hidden choices that make results diverge. From prompting AI → governing scientific workflows.

Divergence narrows to agreement400 runs · conceptual
Rung 05 · Adaptive governance Collaborative research

“How do management plans keep pace with the science, instead of going stale?”

A management plan can run 300 pages and take years — then go stale as knowledge grows. ChatMPA treats it as a living scientific workflow: institutional sections from templates, contextual sections built from monitoring and remote sensing, and strategic sections — zoning, objectives, governance — kept firmly under expert judgment. From static management plans → living conservation intelligence.

The plan, assembled by mode3 modes · conceptual

Home · Mission

Strengthen how the ocean is decided.

ChatMPA exists to close the distance between what marine science knows and what marine decisions reflect — so human judgment can be as strong as the evidence behind it.

The challenge

Not too little science. Too little reach for the science we have.

Decades of monitoring, millions of records, and peer-reviewed methods already exist. But the people responsible for protected areas often cannot reach that knowledge in time, in a form they can defend, when a decision is in front of them. The bottleneck is no longer discovery. It is the pathway from evidence to action.

What we are building toward

Mission, vision, and promise.

Mission

Strengthen how Marine Protected Areas are managed by making scientific knowledge accessible, connected, transparent, and trusted — so human decisions can be as strong as the evidence behind them.

Vision

A world where every marine conservation decision can draw on the full weight of scientific knowledge, and the distance between evidence and action has effectively disappeared.

Purpose

To close the gap between what marine science knows and what marine decisions reflect. That gap — not a lack of data, not a lack of care — is the constraint ChatMPA exists to remove.

Promise

Every answer is traceable to evidence, reviewed by experts, and offered in service of a human decision — never in place of one. What ChatMPA gives you, you can defend.

The category

Scientific decision infrastructure.

Infrastructure is the layer institutions build on and come to depend on. It is invisible when it works, and it outlives any single product built upon it. ChatMPA is that missing layer between marine science and marine decisions.

The word scientific constrains the word decision — accountable to evidence, reproducible, and open to review. That constraint is what separates ChatMPA from a chatbot, a dashboard, or a map.

The philosophy

Human judgment leads. AI strengthens the process.

A division of responsibility that never changes.

ScientistsvalidateGuarantee the reasoning is sound and uncertainty is stated honestly.
← the leadManagersdecideWeigh the trade-offs and own the choice.

What success means

Measured in decisions, not downloads.

If ChatMPA succeeds, marine decisions will get better — not because it made them, but because the people who did had the full weight of scientific knowledge behind them, and the confidence to act on it. Management plans stay current. Agencies defend every choice with a clear line back to the evidence. The oceans, cumulatively and durably, are better protected.

Marine Protected Areas do not need more disconnected information. They need a trusted system that transforms scientific knowledge into better decisions — and keeps learning from the results.

Five connected layers · one continuous structure · human judgment leads throughout

The architecture

Five layers. One continuous structure.

Scientific knowledge enters at the base and rises — each layer transforming the one below it — until it reaches the people and institutions who decide. Then what they learn returns to the base, and the system grows more capable.

  1. Scientific knowledge becomes integrated ecosystem understanding.
  2. Understanding becomes decision support.
  3. Decision support becomes trustworthy through expert governance.
  4. Trusted evidence strengthens adaptive management.
  5. Adaptive management creates new knowledge — and the loop closes.

Scroll — the outline fills in, one layer at a time.

Layer 01AI assists · experts define

Scientific memory

Fragmented records become one accessible, governed memory — and every item keeps its provenance, so any answer can be traced back to its source.

  • Publications
  • Monitoring records
  • Fisheries databases
  • Official datasets & plans
  • Local & expert knowledge
  • Provenance & metadata

From fragmented records → accessible scientific memory.

In practice a Model Context Protocol lets anyone query Mexico's official fisheries database — 10M+ landing records — in plain language (“which species' landings rose over the past decade?”), with no SQL or statistics required and full traceability.

Layer 02AI reasons · scientists frame the questions

Ecosystem intelligence

Independent monitoring streams connect into one framework, so change can be reasoned about across drivers — testing competing explanations instead of reading one variable at a time.

  • Long-term monitoring
  • Biomass & trophic structure
  • Temperature & productivity
  • Habitat
  • Climate signals
  • Uncertainty

From independent monitoring → integrated ecosystem understanding.

In practice nearly three decades of reef monitoring, linked with NASA Earth-observation data.

Layer 03← the human decides

Decision intelligence

Understanding becomes options. The system lays out alternatives, their consequences, and their trade-offs — with uncertainty stated plainly. It does not choose. The manager does.

  • Scenario evaluation
  • Trade-offs
  • The limiting dimension
  • Ecological · economic · social
  • Cost-effectiveness
  • Uncertainty

From understanding change → evaluating possible actions.

In practice the Marine Prosperity Index surfaces the single dimension limiting prosperity, and compares interventions.

Layer 04experts validate

Trustworthy AI

A validation layer wraps everything below it. Expert-built Skills fix the method, the seeds, and the checks; results are versioned, reviewed, and approved before they are ever allowed to reach a decision.

  • Expert Skills
  • Reproducibility vs validity
  • Method contracts
  • Versioning & provenance
  • Peer review
  • Studio

From open-ended AI outputs → governed scientific workflows.

Studio the scientific governance layer — it reviews and validates AI-assisted work the way science governs its own methods. How Studio works →

Layer 05institutions govern

Adaptive governance

Validated evidence reaches managers, directors, rangers, and institutions — who decide, act, and keep learning. Plans evolve with the science instead of going stale, and monitoring returns to the base.

  • MPA managers & directors
  • Rangers & scientists
  • Institutions
  • Management plans
  • Iterative learning
  • Policy implementation

From static planning → adaptive governance.

The loop closes what managers monitor and learn re-enters scientific memory — the system does not end in a one-way recommendation, it ends in learning.

Home · Innovation

Five capabilities. One system, climbing.

Not a portfolio of projects — a ladder of capability, from accessible knowledge to governed decisions. Each rung is built on the one below it.

Rung 01 · Scientific memory Operational

Democratizing Mexico's fisheries knowledge.

From isolated fisheries records → accessible scientific knowledge.

Challenge

Mexico's official fisheries database holds more than 10 million landing records in a complex relational structure — one of the world's largest fisheries datasets. Using it has demanded database knowledge, statistical training, and programming skills, leaving it out of reach for most scientists, managers, practitioners, and decision-makers.

Our innovation

A dedicated Model Context Protocol that understands the database structure and lets anyone interrogate it in natural language — “which species' landings rose over the past decade?”, “what were the most important fisheries in the Gulf of California last year?” — with no SQL, schemas, or statistical software, and full scientific traceability. A scientific interface to the data, not a chatbot.

Why it matters

It democratizes scientific access to one of the world's largest fisheries knowledge systems — shortening the distance between decades of records and the scientists, managers, and communities who need them, without diluting rigor or traceability.

What it demonstrates

Scientists supply ecological understanding and the limits of official statistics; engineers turn that into infrastructure; AI does the computation. Expertise guarantees interpretation.

Next milestone · extend coverage and connect to ecosystem indicators. Requires scientific review

Rung 02 · Ecosystem intelligence Active research

Ecosystem intelligence for decision-making.

From fragmented monitoring → ecosystem intelligence.

Challenge

MPAs respond to many interacting drivers — climate, productivity, habitat, fishing — monitored by programs that rarely communicate, so managers receive fragments instead of an integrated picture.

Our innovation

Specialized connectors integrate nearly three decades of ecological monitoring with Earth-observation data (sea-surface temperature, productivity, marine heatwaves), so AI can reason across them in one scientific framework.

Why it matters

It moves managers beyond descriptive monitoring toward evidence-based adaptive management — explaining why an ecosystem is changing, not just that it changed.

What it demonstrates

A system that tests competing explanations rather than reporting a single trend — with scientists defining questions, evaluating evidence, and owning interpretation.

Status · analytical framework in active research; integration into workflows underway. Requires scientific review

Rung 03 · Decision intelligence Active research

From measuring conservation to guiding decisions.

From measuring sustainability → navigating prosperity.

Challenge

Conservation choices affect ecology, economy, and society at once, yet these are usually evaluated separately — leaving trade-offs invisible and most indices able to say where a place stands, not what to do next.

Our innovation

The Marine Prosperity Index evaluates how environment, economy, and society interact, identifies the dimension limiting prosperity, and simulates alternative pathways as decision-support cards.

Why it matters

Conservation is ultimately choice. Surfacing the limiting dimension and the trade-offs helps managers prioritize investment with evidence instead of guesswork.

What it demonstrates

Turning static scores into navigable pathways — the shift from measurement to guidance, always under human decision authority.

Status · framework in active research. Requires scientific review

Rung 04 · Trustworthy scientific AI Controlled experiment

Expert Skills for trustworthy scientific AI.

From prompting AI → governing scientific workflows.

Challenge

AI can be perfectly consistent and consistently wrong. Ask the same question two ways and answers diverge — unacceptable when a real decision depends on them.

Our innovation

Methodological judgment is encoded into structured, reviewable Skills — the unit of analysis, the method, the seeds, the checks. A controlled experiment across 400 runs, two languages, and five detail levels shows the right Skill removes the hidden choices that make results diverge.

Why it matters

It is the difference between an impressive answer and a defensible one — the foundation of trust for every capability above and below it.

What it demonstrates

That AI workflows can be governed the way science governs its own methods — reproducible, reviewable, and accountable. This is the work that Studio makes operational.

Status · controlled experiment; governance layer in development. Requires scientific review

Rung 05 · Adaptive governance Collaborative research

AI-assisted adaptive management for MPAs.

From static management plans → living conservation intelligence.

Challenge

A management plan can run hundreds of pages and take years to produce — then go stale as knowledge grows. Many protected areas operate without a current plan.

Our innovation

Treat the plan as a living workflow: institutional sections from templates, contextual sections built from monitoring and remote sensing, and strategic sections — zoning, objectives, governance — kept firmly under expert judgment.

Why it matters

Plans that evolve with the evidence, while institutions keep full legal authority — a credible path for the many MPAs that lack a current one.

What it demonstrates

A clear distinction between automated, data-assisted, and human-guided work — the whole ladder, applied to the instrument that governs a protected area.

Status · collaborative research. Requires scientific review · plan-prevalence figures requires scientific review

Each rung raises the trust of the next.

Home · Studio

Scientific governance for AI-assisted work.

Studio reviews, validates, and strengthens AI-assisted scientific workflows before information ever reaches a decision-maker — the way science governs its own methods. It is not a separate product; it is the accountability layer inside ChatMPA.

Why it exists

AI can be perfectly consistent — and consistently wrong.

Most AI systems optimize for a fluent answer. A real conservation decision needs a defensible one. Studio exists because an answer that cannot be traced, reproduced, and reviewed has no place in a decision that affects an ecosystem, a community, and public resources for decades.

The workflow

Draft, review, validate, approve.

Nothing reaches a decision-maker until it has passed through governance.

01DraftAI assembles an answer, integrating and synthesizing the evidence.
02ReviewExperts examine the method, the assumptions, and the uncertainty.
03ValidateReproducibility and validity are tested — deliberately, as two different things.
04ApproveOnly then does an answer reach a decision-maker — accountable, and traceable.

Reproducible is not the same as valid

Reproducible
Valid

A result can be perfectly repeatable and still wrong — until the scientific unit of analysis is defined. Studio treats the two as distinct, which is one of the rarest and most credible things a scientific system can say.

Governance, in practice

Expertise, made shared and reviewable.

A Skill turns scientific method from undocumented personal practice into shared, citable infrastructure.

Authorship & versioning

Every Skill has an author, a version history, and a change record — like a method, not a prompt.

Testing & tolerances

Reference outputs and tolerances catch drift, so the same question yields the same grounded answer.

Provenance

Every result traces back to its evidence, so a decision-maker can follow the line from claim to source.

Peer review

Skills carry a path to review, so methods are scrutinized before they inform real decisions.

Stated limits

Known limitations are declared, not hidden — honesty about uncertainty is part of the method.

Expert collaboration

Skills are built and maintained by working scientists, accumulating expertise across institutions.

How Studio fits

Inside the workflow, not beside it.

Studio is the governance layer that sits within the primary ChatMPA workflow — the checkpoint every AI-assisted answer passes through before it reaches a manager. It is not a separate ecosystem, an independent product, a generic workspace, or a second platform. It is what makes the human-led principle structural rather than aspirational.

Because governance runs through everything, trust is not a claim on this page — it is a property of the system.
